name: Hepher
overview: Hepher is identified in Scripture both as a person and a place, illustrating the interconnectedness of lineage and land in God's covenant people. Hepher was a son of Gilead and an ancestor of Zelophehad, whose daughters notably inherited his estate due to the absence of sons, emphasizing God's provision and justice within family inheritance (Numbers 26:32-33; Numbers 27:1; Joshua 17:2-3). Additionally, Hepher is named as a city west of the Jordan River, reflecting the territorial allotments given to the tribes of Israel (Joshua 12:17). This dual reference underscores the significance of Hepher in biblical history as both a familial line and a geographical location within the Promised Land.
